photos.description:
Nimikon Falls, the river splits around an island with most of the flow to the right.  The main sequence of falls is just above where the river makes a sharp left hand corner, there is a house in the woods on the right.  There is a left line with a tougher set up through numerous holes and a right line down a sloping drop into a deep pool.
(started at 2' on visual gauge at south boundary rd., ended run with 1' on visual gauge at south boundary rd.)

detail.description:
Reach includes Minnewawa Falls and Nimikon Falls.

Some fine video of this run is available at: [https://youtu.be/nk85E9flJEM](https://youtu.be/nk85E9flJEM)

Put-in: broken bridge on Underwood Tower Road

Take-out: Steigers Bridge on logging road

Note: Getting shuttle vehicles down to the listed take-out at Steigers Bridge may not be available due to the logging road being closed (gated). This may necessitate continuing downstream to run the [Lower Presque](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/940/). This makes a long day, paddling a total of 15.7 miles (or 16.8 to the mouth, including the 'final mile' or [Bottom Presque](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/2643/) run).

Note: There is about 16 miles of low gradient river from the listed take-out of the prior (upper section) to the put-in for this section.

[Click here for Part 1 of an article from the AW Journal, way back in 1981](https://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/Journal/show-page/issue/4/year/1981/page/17/)!

[Click here for Part 2 of the article](https://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/Journal/show-page/issue/5/year/1981/page/14/).

The article describes the following: Michigan's, [Upper Presque Isle](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/939/), [Lower Presque Isle](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/940/), [Middle Black](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/928/), [Lower Black](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/2640/), [Upper Silver](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/2593/),  [Lower Silver](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/2594/), [Falls](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/2592/), and [Rock](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/2602/); and Wisconsin's [Lower Brunsweiler](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/2753/), [Montreal Canyon](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/2301/), and [West Branch Montreal](https://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/2300/).

correlationDetails.belowRecommendedRangeComment: 0 - 2.5 Ft. Almost certainly too low. 2.5 - 2.8 Ft. Most likely too low, but possibly E.L.F. (extreme low flow) run.
correlationDetails.aboveRecommendedRangeComment: 5 - 10 Ft. Likely too high. *** 10 - 20 Ft. Likely extremely high and perhaps dangerous.

correlationDetails.aboveRecommendedRangeComment: All ranges are highly tentative! Please post a trip report stating gauge reading and your impression (too low, low runnable, moderate runnable, high runnable, or dangerously high).
